issues.legal_issue: A State cannot require a constituent medical college of an independent university established under a separate State law to obtain affiliation from another university through a law directed to admissions and fee regulation.
material_facts: The university was established under a separate State enactment and had powers to establish constituent colleges, conduct examinations, and confer degrees.
The medical college was established and permitted to operate as a constituent college of that university.
An amendment to the State law governing admissions and fee fixation required private medical educational institutions in the State to obtain affiliation from a different university.
The college and university challenged the mandatory external-affiliation requirement, and the college’s status as a constituent of the university was undisputed.
issues.conclusion: The mandatory external-affiliation provision was irrational, unreasonable, and unconstitutional because it intruded on the autonomy of the independent university. The provision was struck down, and the authorities were directed to proceed without requiring the constituent college to obtain affiliation from the other university.
issues.legal_principle: The separate university enactment empowered the university to establish constituent colleges and provided for its independent academic functions, including examinations and degrees. A constituent college is an integral part of its university. The State law concerning admissions and fee fixation could regulate those matters but could not displace the authority of the university governing affiliation of its own constituent college. The requirement also infringed the university’s autonomy and was held contrary to Articles 14 and 19(1)(g) of the Constitution. The Court did not rely on an earlier case for this dispositive conclusion; it noted that the High Court had discussed earlier cases distinguishing recognition from affiliation but said it need not dilate on that distinction.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_appeal and independent_university_under_separate_law and constituent_college and mandatory_affiliation_to_another_university and (university_controls_its_constituent_colleges or enactment_limited_to_admissions_and_fees)

predicates.constitutional_challenge_appeal: A party brings an appeal challenging the constitutionality of a requirement imposed on a medical college.
predicates.independent_university_under_separate_la: The college’s university was established under a separate law and operates as an independent university.
predicates.constituent_college: The medical college is an integral constituent of that university.
predicates.mandatory_affiliation_to_another_univers: A State requirement compels the constituent college to obtain affiliation from a university other than its own.
predicates.university_controls_its_constituent_coll: The university has authority to establish or govern its constituent colleges and to conduct their examinations or confer their qualifications.
predicates.enactment_limited_to_admissions_and_fees: The enactment imposing the requirement is directed to regulating admissions and fees rather than establishing universities or governing affiliation.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a mandatory external-affiliation requirement for a constituent medical college of an independent university, and the university governs its constituent colleges or the requirement is imposed through an enactment limited to admissions and fees, the requirement is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A condition in an administrative certificate cannot compel compliance with an unconstitutional requirement to obtain affiliation from another university.
material_facts: The State had issued an essentiality certificate for establishing the medical college subject to compliance with the law governing private medical institutions.
The later affiliation requirement compelled the university’s constituent college to seek affiliation from another university.
The Court held that the affiliation requirement was unconstitutional and intruded on the university’s autonomy.
issues.conclusion: The certificate condition did not bind the university to comply with an unconstitutional and onerous affiliation requirement.
issues.legal_principle: An administrative condition attached to an essentiality certificate cannot validate or enforce a requirement that is unconstitutional and impinges on the autonomy protected by the separate university enactment and Articles 14 and 19(1)(g) of the Constitution. No earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_appeal: A party brings an appeal challenging the constitutionality of a requirement imposed on a medical college.
predicates.certificate_condition: An administrative certificate for establishing the college states that the college or university must comply with specified requirements.
predicates.condition_requires_unconstitutional_exte: The certificate condition is invoked to require affiliation from another university, and that affiliation requirement is unconstitutional.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an unconstitutional external-affiliation requirement and a certificate condition is invoked to enforce it, the condition cannot require that affiliation.
